story: Saturday evening in Sumter Oaks finds the humid October air hanging hazy over Magnolia Loop, where Gary and Donna are walking together with a warm peach cobbler, Donna already promising a dink session at the rec center tomorrow morning. Rosa is waiting at her house with the table set and cornbread ready, calling Donna and Gary in for dinner while Hal squares up the dining table. Everyone is content and cheerful as the golf carts slow down along the street and the whole neighborhood settles in for supper.
events: Hal (rosa dining table): Square the table up and set the cornbread on it, ready for dinner

gary.thought_process: Rosa already invited me in and told me where the chairs and ice go, and I said I'd carry things over. Donna just got here, and Rosa is holding her seat. I've said my piece about the cart already, so no need to repeat it. The helpful thing is to stop standing around on the Loop and take the ice and chairs through to Rosa's kitchen. The cart stays in the garage until the review board signs off, and Saturday dinner with Rosa and Donna is what I've been looking forward to.

parameters.content: Heading into Rosa's with the ice and chairs for dinner, like she asked.

donna.thought_process: I'm on Magnolia Loop at 7:17 PM and both Gary and Rosa are right here. Gary left me waiting on the court, but he's here now and Rosa's Saturday dinner is the plan. I already told him about the booked slot, so I shouldn't repeat that. Better to be gracious, get the group moving toward Rosa's, and mention the cobbler. I can nudge Gary about a practice session at the rec center tomorrow to keep the ladder goal moving.

parameters.content: Gary, there you are! I've got the peach cobbler warming, so let's walk over to Rosa's together. And tomorrow morning you and I are hitting dinks at the rec center, no excuses.

hal.thought_process: I'm at Rosa's House now, and no one's in line-of-sight. Gary's already come and gone through the kitchen, I gather, and Donna isn't here yet. My notebook's been tidied and the old notices cleared, so I've no complaints to file tonight. Rosa's dinner is what matters, and the cornbread and table ought to be dealt with without fuss. The dining table is right here, so the sensible thing is to see it's set properly and in good order for Donna's seat and the rest of the neighbors. Soft-hearted or not, a man shows up and makes himself useful.

parameters.content: Square the table up and set the cornbread on it, ready for dinner

rosa.thought_process: It's 7:17 PM and the dinner was set for six, so Gary and Donna are both here on the Loop with me and Hal has headed to my house. I already told Gary to come in and Donna just arrived, so I shouldn't repeat my invitation to Gary. Best move is to get everyone to the table: speak to Donna, the one who just arrived, and tell her the cobbler goes through the kitchen and her seat is waiting. Gary can follow along naturally. Everyone at one table is exactly what I've wanted since the move.

parameters.content: Donna, there you are! Bring that cobbler straight through to the kitchen, Hal's already headed in and your seat is waiting. Gary, grab the ice and follow us, the table's set.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
